Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

precmed 1.1.0.9000 (development version)

Major changes

  • Count atefit() now always fits separate outcome models by treatment arm, without the previous fallback to a pooled model for small arms. The interactions argument has been removed from ATE fitting, including the option for a pooled model without interactions. This is a breaking change: calls using interactions must be updated, and positional arguments that followed it have shifted. Results and bootstrap inference can change.

  • Added support for binary outcomes on the risk-difference scale to atefit(), catefit(), and catecv(), including doubly robust estimation, logistic and boosting scores, cross-validated subgroup estimates, and a new vignette. Binary atefit() fits separate logistic outcome models by treatment arm. Binary cross-validation uses treatment-stratified splits rather than the balanced-split controls error.max and max.iter.

  • Standardized bootstrap failure handling across binary, count and survival atefit(): affected measures now have unavailable inference if any replicate fails or is undefined, instead of silently omitting count replicates. Results record replicate-level reasons in bootstrap.diagnostics and diagnostics().

  • Added the population-level log.cumulative.hazard.ratio at tau0 to survival atefit(), with bootstrap inference. Inference is unavailable if the estimate or any bootstrap replicate is undefined. This replaces the conditional Cox log.hazard.ratio in atefit() output, a breaking change. Subgroup and validation conditional HR outputs remain available as hr.*; their values can change because of the horizon correction described below.

  • Added subgroup cumulative hazard ratios to survival catefit() and catecv() as chr.* outputs; hr.* outputs remain conditional Cox hazard ratios. Survival plots and box plots now accept measure = "rmtl" (default), "cumulative_hr", or "conditional_hr"; validation curves can display multiple measures. The previously supported plot.hr argument is deprecated; plot.hr = TRUE now selects the cumulative hazard ratio by default rather than the conditional Cox HR. Use measure = "conditional_hr" to plot the latter. Older saved objects must be refitted for cumulative hazard plots.

  • Added C backends, enabled by default, for count and survival contrast regression, Cox restricted mean survival integration, and LASSO propensity-score interaction screening. Installing from source now requires a C compiler and R’s standard BLAS/LAPACK libraries.

  • Added contrast.control, rmst.control, and ps.control for numerical backend settings. Set solver = "R" to use the R implementation; small floating-point differences between backends are possible.

  • Replaced gbm with gbm3 for boosting models. Existing tuning argument names and the learning rate of 0.1 are preserved; stored fits now have class GBMFit. Results can differ even with identical settings and random seeds.

  • Added simulate_count(), simulate_binary(), and simulate_survival() to generate reproducible synthetic data for illustrating and testing the package’s methods with confounding and heterogeneous treatment effects.

Minor changes

  • Split the binary, count and survival worked examples into separate ATE and CATE vignettes. Existing example URLs continue to lead to the ATE guides; the README and vignette navigation link to both guides for each outcome.

  • Survival atefit() supports outcome_method = "weibull" and "log_normal" (alias "lognormal") in addition to the default Cox outcome model. Arm-specific accelerated failure time models supply RMST and horizon survival predictions. The Weibull model allows different shapes by arm; the log-normal model does not impose proportional hazards. Censoring models remain controlled separately by ipcw.method and ipcw.model.

  • atefit() now accepts outcome_method: count outcomes use "poisson" by default and also support "negative_binomial" (alias "negbin"). Binary and survival outcomes accept "logistic" and "coxph", respectively. Negative binomial outcome models are refitted in each bootstrap sample; their estimates and uncertainty can differ from Poisson-based results. The new argument follows outcome_model; calls placing the treatment-model formula immediately after the outcome formula remain supported.

  • atefit() and outcome-specific ATE functions now use outcome_model for the outcome formula. The former named argument cate.model remains a deprecated alias and emits a warning; supplying both arguments is an error. The help describes how the outcome models handle treatment. See the major change above for the removal of interactions and its positional impact.

  • init.model can specify separate initial outcome-model covariates for twoReg and contrastReg across supported outcome types in fitting and validation. It defaults to cate.model. Continuous-outcome fitting and validation remain unavailable.

  • Boosting performance plots are now disabled by default in model fitting and cross-validation. Set plot.gbmperf = TRUE to display them.

  • Exported catefitbinary() as the binary-outcome counterpart to catefitcount() and catefitsurv(), with a dedicated help page.

  • Expanded the catefit() help to compare CATE score methods and explain which use doubly robust estimation and their qualifications.

  • Added a package-level overview accessible with ?precmed, including a short example, effect scales, and links to online guides and the handbook.

  • Added an introductory vignette explaining doubly robust estimation, propensity score weighting, outcome-model standardization (g-computation), their assumptions, and their use in precmed.

  • Added subgroup_estimates() to extract nested binary, count and survival subgroup estimates by scoring method and measure. Newly fitted survival catefit() objects also retain subgroup treatment-specific risks and RMSTs and risk differences.

  • Added predict(), coef() and confint() methods for catefit score extraction. Predictions return stored analysis-sample scores; coefficient intervals require available contrast-regression standard errors and are not available for survival fits.

  • Survival atefit() bootstrap plots group RMST, risks and the cumulative hazard ratio by row by default; metrics still controls selection and order and accepts underscore spellings of dotted metric names.

  • Survival catecv() now stores subgroup risk differences at tau0; validation plots support measure = "risk_difference"; dotted measure names are available as aliases.

  • Survival atefit() now reports treatment-specific event risks and their difference at tau0, with bootstrap inference and plot support.

  • diagnostics(fit, type = "propensity") now reports full-sample propensity score overlap, truncation, inverse treatment weights and effective sample sizes for newly fitted binary, count and survival atefit() results. The default message table is unchanged. Overlap diagnostics now default to a compact formatted table; use layout = "arms" or layout = "metrics" for unrounded numeric results; type = "overlap" remains an alias.

  • Binary atefit() bootstrap plots now display the treatment-specific risks and risk difference by default. metrics selects and orders risk0, risk1, and risk.difference. Older objects without risk bootstrap estimates retain the risk-difference plot.

  • Added plot() support for catefit score distributions, with histograms, optional density curves, method selection, and a configurable reference line. The score axis uses the original treatment labels when available; newly fitted catefit objects retain these labels, while older fits use treatment 0/1. Binary, count and survival vignettes now use this method.

  • The binary vignette compares logistic and two-regression scores on the same internal validation splits, uses 10 iterations and larger subgroups to reduce rank-deficient fits, removes the redundant manual validation example, and explains the printed average treatment effect before showing extraction and plotting commands.

  • Standardized documentation terminology for outcome, treatment and censoring models, clarifying propensity scores and inverse probability of censoring weights.

  • Clarified binary, count and survival outcome support in the package description, README, quick start and function documentation. The README and introductory vignettes also describe survival risk differences and distinguish their scale from survival CATE scores. The quick start presents the estimated count rate ratio and confidence interval in a concise table.

  • Added an ATE methods vignette covering binary, count and survival outcomes, assumptions and bootstrap inference; the CATE methods vignette separates score development from validation.

  • Added combine to abc() to aggregate cross-validation iterations per scoring method with a mean, median, or user-supplied function. The default still returns the full matrix; missing values are not removed automatically.

  • Added a dashed null reference line to count and survival atefit() bootstrap log-ratio plots. null.value defaults to 0 on the log scale and can be set to another value, NULL, or NA; treatment-specific RMST panels are unchanged.

  • Count atefit() now retains bootstrap rate estimates and treatment labels; its bootstrap plot displays rates for both treatments alongside the log rate ratio. Older saved fits continue to display the log-ratio panel only.

  • Added metrics to plot.atefit() to select and order available bootstrap metrics by their names in the fitted object.

  • Improved bootstrap histogram styling with a minimal default theme and panel headings, and added a caption explaining the estimate and null reference lines. Supply theme to use another ggplot2 theme. Histogram bars now default to alpha = 1 so the background grid does not show through them.

  • Applied the same default theme to validation curves and subgroup box plots; their theme argument still accepts a custom ggplot2 theme. Captions explain the dashed overall treatment effect reference lines. Multi-measure survival plots use horizontal panel headings and matched y scales within each measure. Set show.overall = FALSE on validation curves or box plots to hide the overall effect line. Validation curves accept layout = "method" to compare training and validation curves within method-specific panels. Subgroup box plots now default to two columns; ncol controls their layout.

  • Validate outcome types and outcome-specific CATE scoring methods before fitting, including empty and invalid inputs.

  • Added catecvCountExample, a pre-fitted validation result used in the ABC and plotting examples to avoid repeatedly fitting models.

  • Label survival atefit() bootstrap plot panels with the original treatment names when available, and use readable names for the treatment effects.

  • Report automatic treatment recoding as an informational message rather than a warning, while retaining the mapping in existing result objects.

  • Added diagnostics() to summarize recorded survival atefit() treatment recoding information and subgroup errors and warnings from catefit() and catecv() results in a data frame.

  • Added coef() and confint() methods for extracting supported treatment effects and confidence intervals from count and survival atefit() results.

  • Improved performance of balanced splitting, continuous contrast regression, censoring probability calculations, and propensity-score LASSO fitting.

  • Updated validation plots and box plots for current ggplot2 and tidyselect versions; ggplot2 >= 3.4.0 is now required.

  • Added the book chapter by Jiang et al. (2026) to the package description and references.

  • Added Smart Data Analysis and Statistics B.V. as copyright holder for its contributions after version 1.1.0, alongside the existing Biogen attribution.

Bug fixes

  • Fixed atefit() argument evaluation for count and survival data supplied from a local calling environment.

  • Fixed continuous boosting predictions by retaining the selected tree count for each treatment arm, and forwarding additional boosting controls.

  • Fixed survival Cox hazard ratios to censor follow-up at tau0 instead of treating observations beyond the horizon as events. This affects subgroup and cross-validation hazard ratio estimates; this correction does not change the RMST and RMTL calculations.

  • Fixed survival random forest event coding at tau0 and integrated predicted survival curves through the full horizon when computing RMST. Survival forest scores and scores using forest initial predictions may change.

  • Warn when an out-of-range doubly robust RMST estimate is replaced by an outcome-model estimate, including when this occurs during bootstrap inference.

  • Fixed intercept-only propensity models in survival cross-fitting, subgroup evaluation, and bootstrap ATE estimation by preserving matrix dimensions.

  • Fixed LASSO propensity-score dimension handling with two predictors or a single prediction row.

  • Return NA with an informative warning for count-outcome responder subgroups missing one or both treatment arms, instead of failing the analysis. ABC is NA when a required validation estimate is unavailable.

  • Use GBM3 cross-validation for single-predictor count boosting fits and boosting initial predictions, removing the legacy out-of-bag workaround and fixing a cross-fitting error when selecting the number of trees.

  • Removed a duplicate treated-arm boosting fit in count cross-fitting. Results obtained with the same seed may change because fewer random draws are consumed.

precmed 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2024-10-05

  • Removed dependency on the MESS package.
  • Fixed an issue in the cross-validation procedure that lead to an increased total sample size
  • Updated documentation using roxygen2 (version 7.3.2) and resolved bracketing issues.

precmed 1.0.0.9000

  • Added a NEWS.md file to track changes to the package.
